resources.string: An openwork sphere lookout on Várdomb in Balatonboglár, built for the 1958 Brussels World’s Fair and now overlooking Lake Balaton.
A scenic promenade along Fonyód’s high shore, with views across Lake Balaton toward the volcanic hills of the north shore.
A panoramic terrace in the wooded Kishegy above Balatonlelle, among vineyards and woodland with views over Lake Balaton.
A lookout on the vineyard-covered Kőhegy above Zamárdi. The tower stands on the site of a former abbey press house, with views across Lake Balaton.
A promenade along the high shore at Balatonvilágos, following a green public space above the eastern basin of Lake Balaton.
A nature trail through the protected Cinege-stream valley, passing ponds, wetlands, woodland and birdwatching spots.
Medieval castle ruins on the forested 283-metre Várhegy above Kereki. Remains of the walls and gate tower stand within the former moat.
A viewpoint near the Kőröshegyi viaduct, one of Central Europe’s longest road bridges, with views of the bridge and surrounding hills.
A 124-metre elevated path among hornbeam and oak crowns, connected to a woodland nature trail with information about forest wildlife.
A lake near Kaposvár with shoreline paths, an arboretum and a canopy walkway, with routes passing woodland and waterside habitats.
An otter park among woodland ponds in Somogy, with rescued animals and surrounding wetland habitats observed from the walking path.
A former farm railway from Balatonfenyves to Somogyszentpál and Csisztafürdő. The line crosses the meadows and pastures of the Nagyberek.
A forest railway at Kaszó, in the largest continuous woodland of Inner Somogy. The line runs through forest near the protected Baláta-tó.
An adventure park on Balatonboglár’s Vár-domb, next to the Gömbkilátó. It has an alpine coaster, rope course, free-fall tower and archery.
A stepped travertine waterfall in the Szalajka Valley, visible from the streamside walking path through the beech woodland.
A stalactite cave in Lillafüred with large chambers and limestone columns. Guided tours follow a developed visitor route.
A waterfall beside the palace hotel in Lillafüred, where the Szinva drops over a rock face, visible from the surrounding walking paths.
A scenic mountain lake in Lillafüred, surrounded by steep forested slopes and popular walking routes.
A rare limestone cave in Lillafüred, known for its natural tufa formations and long tourist history.
A rocky viewpoint on the southern edge of the Bükk Plateau, overlooking the wooded valleys of the southern Bükk from a steep cliff.
A limestone crag on the southern edge of the Bükk Plateau, reached on forest trails, with views across the ridges and valleys below.
A bare limestone mountain above Bélapátfalva, with traces of former mining and panoramic views.
The most popular hiking valley of the Bükk, with springs, lakes and the Fátyol Waterfall.
A cave famous for its prehistoric site, with archaeological finds and strict protection.
A highly protected cave in the Bükk, known for prehistoric archaeological finds. Its broad entrance is reached on a woodland walk.
A long wooded valley in the Bükk with cliffs, caves and springs. Paths along the valley connect to several mountain hiking routes.
Castle ruins above Szarvaskő beside the National Blue Trail, with views of the village and surrounding mountains from the remaining walls.
Volcanic tuff rocks with carved niches in the Bükk foothills. Their purpose remains uncertain; the rocks have archaeological significance.
A lake surrounded by wooded hills in Felsőtárkány, with a lakeside walking path and nearby forest trails connecting to hikes in the Bükk.
A cave known for prehistoric finds and the Ördögtorony rock in the Hór Valley. Both sites can be included in a walk along the valley.
Volcanic tuff towers with carved niches in Kaptár Valley. A nature trail explains their rock formations and archaeological significance.
A village in the Bükk foothills with wine cellars and routes into the southern Bükk, with village streets that can be explored on foot.
A high-lying 800m tall plateau and spacious meadow on the Bükk Plateau, popular for hiking and relaxation.
The highest point of the Bükk (961 m), in a wooded part of the Bükk Plateau. The summit is reached along forest hiking trails.
An astronomy centre in Répáshuta with a planetarium, meteorites and telescope programmes, and a planetary trail in the surrounding woodland.
Remains of medieval castle walls on a steep rocky summit, reached by a forest path, with views across the northern Bükk from the ruins.
Border fortress above the old town of Eger, defended by István Dobó against the Ottoman siege of 1552. It houses the Dobó István Castle Museum.
A forest railway in the Bükk north of Eger, starting from Felsőtárkány. A game park lies along the line and a nature trail at the terminus.
A forest railway from Miskolc up the Szinva valley to Lillafüred and Garadna. The line passes Lake Hámori and runs through the Bükk forests.
A steep forest railway in the Szalajka valley, from the edge of Szilvásvárad to a clearing above the Fátyol waterfall, with a stop at the fish pond.
A single-tube bobsled track in the forest by the ski slope at the entrance to the Szalajka Valley. It was the first of its type in Hungary.
The highest point of the Mátra and Hungary (1014 m), with a lookout tower overlooking the mountains and surrounding landscape.
A high summit in the Mátra with the Galya lookout tower. The tower overlooks wooded ridges, and several hiking trails lead to the peak.
A wooded stream valley in the Mátra with a waterfall dropping from a rock face. A walking path follows the stream to the waterfall.
A village at the foot of the Mátra beside the Bene stream, with woodland walking routes starting towards the surrounding mountains.
Ruins of Sirok Castle stand on a volcanic cone in the Mátra, with views over the Mátra and Bükk mountains.
A small cave near Disznó-kő in the volcanic rocks of the Mátra. Forest trails lead to the rocky hillside around the cave.
A former mine pit turned into a tarn, with uniquely colored water and wild surroundings.
The highest situated lake of the Mátra, a popular hiking destination with a lookout and nature trail.
The wildest gorge of the Mátra, with rocky terrain and distinctive geological formations. Its woodland path crosses stony ground.
A rocky viewpoint near Kékestető, reached by a woodland path, with views of the mountains and valleys on the northern side of the Mátra.
A rocky viewpoint beside forest hiking trails in the Mátra, overlooking the wooded landscape to the north of the mountain range.
A summit in the Mátra with castle remains, reached by woodland paths, with views of the surrounding mountains from the top.
Castle ruins below the Mátra with a Gothic church tower and carved stones, with historical displays about life on a medieval noble estate.
A scenic railway from the edge of Gyöngyös’s Orczy park on two lines, to Mátrafüred and Szalajkaház. Both climb steeply out of town.
An adventure park on the Mátra’s southern slope above Mátrafüred. A 930 m bobsled, a bridge over the Sástó quarry and a chairlift to Sástó.
A sandstone peak (392 m) with a steep cliff. The ridge overlooks the surrounding hills and the Mátra and Bükk ranges.
A pilgrimage site in a wooded valley with a basilica and springs. A visit can be combined with walks along the surrounding forest paths.
A forested valley with streams, a peaceful spot for hiking and excursions in the Heves–Borsod Hills.
A lake surrounded by wooded hills near Hangony. A walk beside the water gives views of the lake and the forested landscape around it.
Protected landscape with diverse wildlife, rare plant and animal species, and hiking trails.
Three prominent hill peaks in the Heves–Borsod Hills, with panoramic hiking trails and forested surroundings.
A Baroque castle on an island beside the Bódva in Edelény, with the building and its island setting visible during a walk around the site.
The most famous sight of Aggtelek National Park, a monumental dripstone cave with multiple entrances and hiking tours.
The Vörös-tó entrance to Baradla Cave. A guided tour passes through large chambers with limestone columns and other cave formations.
A protected cave near Jósvafő, notable for its dripstone formations and guided underground tours.
A small lake on the edge of Aggtelek near the cave entrance, with a waterside stop on a walk around the village and cave surroundings.
A tarn near Jósvafő in a woodland setting, with coloured water and surrounding trees visible on a walk beside the lake.
Medieval castle ruins on a wooded hill above Szögliget, overlooking the hills and valleys of the surrounding karst landscape.
A stream valley near Jósvafő with woodland paths and nature trails, with routes following the streams and describing local wildlife.
A gorge in the Slovak Karst with steep rock walls, crossed by a walking route between the high cliffs and rock formations.
A unique Árpád-era church with twin sanctuaries, a rare example of medieval architecture.
A former mining lake with unique colors and steep cliffs, popular for hiking and diving.
A striking karst hill above Bódvarákó, famous for its cliffs, caves, and panoramic hiking terrain.
Ruins of a 14th-century Pauline monastery in the Szalonna Hills, reached by a forest path leading to the remaining walls and monastery grounds.
A reservoir among wooded hills with a shoreline walking path, where nesting and migrating birds can be seen beside reed beds and open water.
A lake in a former millstone quarry, enclosed by high rock walls. A path along the rim overlooks the water and traces of quarrying.
A Christ statue on a hill above Tarcal, reached on foot. The viewpoint beside it overlooks vineyards and Tokaj Hill.
A volcanic hill above Tokaj with vineyard-covered slopes, with viewpoints overlooking the Bodrog, the Tisza and the surrounding vineyards.
A panoramic lookout above the Tokaj wine region, with broad views of vineyards and Zemplén hills.
The Rákóczi Castle beside the Bodrog, with the Red Tower and a Renaissance courtyard. Exhibitions cover the castle and family history.
Castle ruins on a hilltop in the Zemplén with surviving walls, overlooking the wooded mountains and valleys of the surrounding area.
A steep rocky crag in the Zemplén woodland. The viewpoint is reached on a forest path and overlooks the ridges and valleys of the range.
The highest Hungarian peak of the Zemplén (895 m), on the Slovak border. The nearby Kis-Milic lookout overlooks the Hegyköz.
A castle on a rocky hill above Füzér, with restored walls and historical exhibitions, and views of the surrounding mountains from the grounds.
A summit beside Nagy-Milic with the Károlyi lookout tower, overlooking Füzér Castle and the wooded hills of the Zemplén.
A pedestrian suspension bridge between two hills above Sátoraljaújhely, with views of the valley below and the surrounding mountains.
Medieval castle ruins on a rocky ridge in the Zemplén, with viewpoints overlooking the surrounding hills from the walls and rock ledge.
A forest railway from Pálháza into the Zemplén woods, via Kishuta and Kőkapu to Rostalló. The 9 km line passes through a tunnel.
An adventure park in Sátoraljaújhely with Hungary’s longest chairlift. A lookout tower stands at its top station; there is a bobsled track too.
Károlyi family palace at the foot of the Zemplén Mountains, rebuilt in Romantic style. Its protected English park is free to enter.
A nature trail at Lake Tisza, reached by boat from Szabics port. The walking route has information about the aquatic habitats of the lake.
A nature trail through wetland habitats, with information about traditional marsh foragers, reed-bed plants and aquatic animals.
A visitor centre at Lake Tisza with aquariums and a lookout tower. Aquatic animals are displayed inside, with lake views from the tower.
A park displaying animals formerly found on the grasslands, including bison, wild horses and cattle resembling aurochs.
Fishponds in the Hortobágy with reed beds and birdwatching spots. Paths along the dikes provide views of migrating and nesting birds.
A park displaying traditional Hungarian domestic breeds, including Hungarian grey cattle, racka sheep and other livestock.
A bird habitat in the northern part of Lake Tisza, with reed beds and open water. Birds and shoreline vegetation can be observed from the water.
A dark sky park in the Hortobágy with low light pollution, where the Milky Way and stars can be observed on clear nights.
A boat-accessed boardwalk at Lake Tisza with reed beds and bird hides. Closed since August 2026 due to low water levels.
A thematic adventure park with labyrinths and interactive games, popular with families.
A Neo-Renaissance castle in Szabadkígyós with ornate rooms and a tower, surrounded by a park with walking paths and old trees.
A historical memorial park with the Feszty panorama. Outdoor exhibits use farm buildings and workshops to describe life on the Great Plain.
An arboretum beside an old Körös river branch, with mature trees and plants from distant regions, connected by walking paths.
A visitor centre and wildlife park in the Körös–Maros National Park, with exhibitions and animals representing the river habitats of the region.
A restored Baroque castle in Gyula with historical exhibitions about the building and the lives of its former residents.
Central Europe\'s only intact lowland brick castle, built in the 15th century. It fell to the Ottomans in the 1566 siege and now houses a museum.
The meeting point of the Körös and Tisza rivers, with a sandy shore. Both rivers are visible, and the size of the beach varies with water level.
A canopy walkway with a lookout tower, exploring the floodplain forests of the Maros River.
A canopy walkway and 15 m lookout tower in Erzsébet Park, Gyomaendrőd, on a 1 km nature trail. Paid entry; closed in rain.
A 314 m canopy walkway in the Karcag forest park, at the end of Liget út. It runs 6 m up among the oaks and is free to visit.
An outdoor model park with replicas of Hungarian castles, churches and palaces, displaying architectural landmarks from a thousand years.
A nature trail about the birdlife of Fehér-tó near Szeged, passing reed beds and fishponds where migrating cranes can be seen in autumn.
A nature trail among wind-shaped sand dunes in the Kiskunság, with boards describing feather-grass meadows and drought-tolerant plants.
A lake formed in an old Danube channel, with beaches and the Kékmoszat nature trail beside reed beds and aquatic habitats.
A nature trail beside the reed beds and marsh meadows of Lake Kolon, with bird hides and boards about herons, reed warblers and rare plants.
An English-style landscape garden beside the River Tisza, with mature oaks, ornamental trees and paths among seasonal flowers.
Romantic palace of the Andrássy family near the Tisza, modelled on French châteaux. Restored in 2023, its halls house exhibitions.
A hand-shaped lookout near Hollókő in the Cserhát hills, with a terrace shaped like a palm overlooking the surrounding countryside.
Part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site, this medieval castle is Hollókő’s main attraction.
A lookout tower on a hill near Alsópetény, rising above the trees, with views of the wooded hills of the Cserhát from the top.
Medieval castle ruins on a wooded hill above Buják. A forest path leads to the remaining walls on a hike through the Cserhát.
A Buddhist centre in Tar with a stupa and prayer flags. A walk around the grounds provides a view of the symbols of the Buddhist tradition.
A Bavarian-style stone lookout near Buják, with architecture resembling a hunting lodge and views over the wooded Cserhát hills.
A narrow rock cleft associated with the legend of Saint Ladislaus, with steep rock walls reached along the surrounding forest paths.
A lookout tower on Tepke Hill in the Cserhát, rising above the trees, with panoramic views of the surrounding hills from the top.
A lake inside a former quarry near Apc, at the foot of the Mátra. A woodland path leads to the water enclosed by rock walls.
Medieval castle ruins on volcanic Szanda Hill, reached by a steep path, with views across the Cserhát and distant mountains from the walls.
Medieval castle ruins on a wooded rocky ridge in the Cserhát. A forest path leads to the walls, with views of the surrounding hills.
Andesite columns on Szanda Hill formed as lava cooled. The exposed rock formations show the volcanic origin of the hill.
A meadow at the foot of Naszály with a nature trail and a suspension bridge, with information about wildlife in the clearing and surrounding forest.
A botanical garden with ponds, walking paths and greenhouses, displaying plants from distant regions and flowers that change with the seasons.
A 652-metre limestone mountain with steep woodland trails and karst features. The nearby Látó-hegy viewpoint overlooks the Danube Bend.
Castle ruins on the Slovak side of the border, overlooking the Medves area. Basalt columns below the castle show its volcanic origins.
Medieval castle ruins on a rocky summit above Salgótarján, with views of the Karancs–Medves landscape from the remaining walls.
A basalt ridge with volcanic bombs and rock formations, with viewpoints overlooking Salgó Castle and the hills of the Medves area.
Central Europe’s largest basalt plateau with famous viewpoints and geological treasures.
The highest peak of the Karancs Hills (729 m), with a lookout tower overlooking Nógrád and the surrounding mountains.
A basalt hill in the Medves area with woodland paths. Its volcanic rocks and forested slopes can be seen on a hike through the woods.
Basalt columns and mining-induced rock fissures near Salgótarján, with views towards the Bükk from the marked walking trail.
The remains of a volcanic vent and a former castle site in Nógrád, with geological features and traces of history around the rock.
An exposed area of pale volcanic tuff near Kazár, cut into grooves by rainwater, with rock shapes showing the volcanic origin of the landscape.
Twenty-million-year-old animal footprints, shark teeth and petrified trunks at Ipolytarnóc, with some remains preserved by volcanic ash.
Seven-million-year-old trunks moved from Bükkábrány to Ipolytarnóc, retaining their original wood from an ancient swamp forest.
A narrow, usually dry gorge with high sediment walls. Pebble layers in the exposed banks are deposits from an ancient river.
A former rock shelter in a sandstone wall near Kishartyán, reached by steps cut into the steep cliff below its entrance.
Medieval castle ruins above Nógrád village, with a surviving tower and walls around an open courtyard overlooking the wooded Börzsöny.
A woodland nature trail around Gyadai Meadow, with information boards about the plants and animals of the forest and meadow.
A hill above the Danube Bend with the Julianus stone lookout, overlooking the curve of the river and the surrounding mountains.
A stone lookout tower on Hegyes-tető, overlooking the Danube Bend and Visegrád Castle, reached by a steep forest path.
The highest point of the Börzsöny (938 m), with a lookout tower and panoramic views of the ridges and valleys of the mountain range.
Nagy-Hideg Hill is a popular hiking destination with a tourist house and winter sports opportunities.
Rock shelter on Szent Mihály Hill near Nagymaros, with traces of human carving. An exposed hillside path leads to its entrance.
The Csarna Valley is a wild and secluded forest, one of the most untouched areas of the Börzsöny.
A rounded rock in the Börzsöny woodland, reached by a forest path. Its shape and exposed rock surfaces can be observed along the walk.
Királyrét is one of the most popular hiking areas in the Börzsöny, with a forest railway, small lake, and family-friendly trails.
A forested summit of the central Börzsöny, reached by classic hiking routes through wild mountain terrain.
Ruins of a historic border fortress on a wooded hill in the Börzsöny, with views of the surrounding mountains from the remaining walls.
The Saint Stephen Church in Nagybörzsöny is located in the historic center of the village and is a prominent landmark due to its architectural significance.
A viewpoint near Nagybörzsöny in the Börzsöny, reached by a woodland walking route, with views of the surrounding mountains.
A viewpoint near Perőcsény in the Börzsöny, reached on woodland trails, with views of the surrounding mountains from the ridge.
Nagy-Koppány is a striking summit in the Börzsöny near Nagybörzsöny, popular among hikers.
A summit near Nagybörzsöny in the Börzsöny, with a viewpoint overlooking the surrounding wooded mountains and valleys.
A rocky viewpoint in the Börzsöny, with views of the surrounding ridges and valleys, reached on a hike through the forest.
A scenic railway in a wooded Börzsöny valley, with locomotives and exhibits about forest transport at the Kemence terminus.
A forest railway from Szob via Márianosztra to Nagyirtáspuszta. It climbs from the Danube into the Börzsöny with switchbacks and loops.
A forest railway between Kismaros on the Danube and Királyrét, the busiest in the Börzsöny. Several hiking trails meet at Királyrét.
A forest railway between Nagybörzsöny and Nagyirtáspuszta, on a former timber and stone line. At Nagyirtáspuszta it connects to the Szob train.
A hillside trail in the Visegrád Hills with views of the Danube Bend, following the wooded slopes between the mountains.
A viewpoint above Visegrád, reached on woodland routes, with views of the Danube Bend and the surrounding mountains.
The Apátkúti Valley near Visegrád is a favorite hiking spot with streams and shady forest trails.
A viewpoint in the Visegrád Hills above the Danube Bend, overlooking the curve of the river and the mountains of the Börzsöny.
Rock towers near Prédikálószék with distinctive formations, with views of the surrounding wooded landscape from the rocky ridge.
Rám Gorge is a wild and adventurous canyon with ladders and bridges along the trail.
Dömörkapu near Szentendre is a narrow valley and hiking spot in the Visegrád Mountains.
Sikárosi Meadow near Pomáz is a pleasant resting and hiking area along local trails.
A forest meadow in the Visegrád Hills where several hiking routes meet, with a clearing for a stop between the valleys and ridges.
Bertényi Miklós Botanical Garden in Visegrád features plant collections with walking paths and educational trails.
Borjúfő near Visegrád is a peak and viewpoint overlooking the Danube and surrounding hills.
Historic castle ruins above Visegrád, with views of the Danube Bend and the surrounding mountains from the walls of the former fortress.
The tip of Szentendre Island, where the two branches of the Danube meet, with views of the river and nearby hills from the pebbly shore.
A rocky stream valley near Pomáz with steep walls and cave openings. The woodland path follows the stony streambed through the gorge.
A small waterfall in a wooded stream valley near Szentendre, reached by a forest path. Its water flow depends on recent rainfall.
A wooded rise near Pilisszentlászló, with paths through the interior of the Visegrád Hills between forested slopes and valleys.
A viewpoint in the Visegrád Hills overlooking the Danube Bend and the Börzsöny. Several woodland hiking routes start nearby.
A viewpoint near Dobogókő overlooking the Danube valley and the Börzsöny, reached on a woodland walking path along the rocky ridge.
A rocky hill near Dömös with views towards the Danube Bend. Forest paths connect it to the surrounding mountain hiking routes.
A meadow in the Visegrád Hills, linked by woodland paths to nearby hiking routes, with an open clearing for a rest during a forest walk.
A rocky ridge above wooded valleys in the Visegrád Hills. Hillside paths lead to the viewpoint over the surrounding mountains.
A pale rock formation on a wooded hillside near Esztergom. Its exposed surfaces and shapes can be seen from the surrounding paths.
A viewpoint on the hill above Esztergom, overlooking the basilica, the Mária Valéria Bridge, the Danube and hills across the river.
A narrow gorge in the Visegrád Hills near Szentendre, with a walking path between steep rock walls on the wooded hillside.
The Esztergom Basilica is Hungary\'s largest church, an imposing architectural landmark.
Árpád-era royal seat on Castle Hill, beside the Basilica. The Castle Museum of the Hungarian National Museum occupies the royal palace remains.
Two bobsled tracks beside the Nagy-Villám lookout above Visegrád: a concrete-channel summer track and an all-weather alpine coaster.
The Egri Castle replica near Pilisborosjenő is a popular hiking spot and film location.
A prominent summit above Pilisborosjenő, popular for its wide panorama and classic day-hike routes.
A rock shelter on the slope of Nagy-Kevély in the Pilis, beside a woodland hiking trail, with an exposed cavity and surrounding rock wall.
The highest peak of the Pilis (756 m), with the Boldog Özséb lookout. The tower overlooks the Pilis and surrounding hills.
A lookout on Pilis-tető built around a former survey tower. It rises above the trees, with views of the Pilis and the surrounding hills.
A limestone rock above Csobánka with views of the village and the Pilis hills, reached by a steep path to an open rocky ledge.
A stone chapel above Pilisszántó, designed by Imre Makovecz and József Őrfi, with curved organic architecture on the hillside.
Sas Rock near Pilisvörösvár is a striking rock formation and a popular hiking spot.
Limestone cave in the Csévi cliffs. Its spacious entrance chambers can be visited without a guide; deeper passages are closed.
Limestone cave beside Leány Cave in the Csévi cliffs. The entrance chambers are open; deeper passages require caving permission.
The Dera Gorge at Pilisszentkereszt features unique rock walls and a stream bed. Family-friendly short walk.
A camel-shaped dolomite rock near Pilisborosjenő at the edge of a former quarry, with exposed rock surfaces beside the surrounding paths.
The Jági trail near Pilisszentiván showcases the flora and fauna of the meadow and stream.
A protected dolomite hill in Budapest with a guided nature trail about its plants, and views of the city and the Buda Hills from the top.
Dolomite rocks above Budapest with woodland paths and viewpoints. The rocky ridge overlooks the surrounding Buda Hills.
A wooded hill above Óbuda with walking paths and limestone outcrops, part of the cave-bearing rocks of the Buda Hills.
A dolomite rock above Budapest with a path around it. The ledge overlooks the Buda Hills and city neighbourhoods in the valleys below.
A hill above the Danube in Budapest with historical monuments. Its walking paths overlook the bridges, Parliament and Buda Castle.
A sculpture garden on Gellért Hill with figures representing world religions, overlooking Buda Castle and the surrounding neighbourhoods.
A mushroom-shaped sandstone rock near Biatorbágy, formed from ancient marine sediment, with views of the surrounding landscape from nearby ledges.
An Ottoman tomb and rose garden in Budapest, with terraces overlooking the Danube and the city. The building dates from the Turkish period.
A wooded hill in Buda with the terminus of the Children's Railway. Walking paths around the station connect forest walks with railway trips.
A wooded valley in Budapest around the Children's Railway station, with paths into the Buda Hills that can be combined with a railway trip.
An outdoor area in Buda with open meadows and woodland walking paths, views of Budapest from the hillside and trails to nearby hills.
The valley of the Paprikás stream near Solymár, with a small waterfall and rock walls. A woodland path runs beside the stream.
Medieval castle remains on Mátyás Hill in Solymár, with information about local history and views of the Buda Hills from the tower.
A stone lookout on Látó Hill beside woodland paths, with a terrace overlooking the Danube, Budapest rooftops and the surrounding Buda Hills.
A valley in Budapest where the Ördög-árok stream runs between limestone walls, with a woodland path beside the stony bed and a cave entrance.
The highest point of Budapest, with the Erzsébet lookout and forest paths. The tower is currently closed; its surroundings remain accessible.
A wooded hill in Buda with the Kaán Károly lookout, reached on walking paths, with views of Budapest and the Buda Hills from the tower.
A dolomite tower on the slope of János Hill. A path around the rock gives views of its formations and the Budapest neighbourhoods below.
Farkas Hill near Budaörs is a popular hiking spot, there is a very nice view of the Törökugrató and the Budaörs Kopárok.
A dolomite clearing on the slope of Nagy-Kopasz with views of the Buda Hills, open grassland and exposed rocks beside woodland paths.
A wooded valley near Budakeszi with paths between shaded hillsides, connecting to the surrounding hiking routes in the Buda Hills.
A forestry arboretum in Budakeszi with a collection of tree and shrub species, connected by walking paths through the planting areas.
An open dolomite summit near Nagykovácsi with panoramic views of the Buda Hills and protected rocky grasslands containing distinctive plants.
A rocky wooded rise near Solymár, with hillside paths between the surrounding hills and exposed rock surfaces along the route.
A wooden lookout on Nagy-Kopasz, rising above the forest, with views of Budapest, the Buda Hills and more distant mountain ranges.
The highest point of the Buda Hills (559 m), with the Csergezán Pál lookout, overlooking the surrounding hills and Budapest.
A visitor section of Budapest's longest cave system, with stalactites, fossil shells and high fissures visible on a guided tour.
A thermal cave in Budapest with pea-shaped mineral clusters and cauliflower-like formations, visited on a guided, paved route.
A railway run by children in the Buda Hills, between Széchenyi-hegy and Hűvösvölgy. Lookouts and hiking trails lie close to its stops.
A medieval church ruin on the hill in Zsámbék, with twin towers and surviving walls showing Romanesque and Gothic architectural details.
Kamalduli monastery in Tata surrounded by forests, calm environment and cultural value.
A boardwalk through a swamp forest in Tata, passing warm springs and clear pools, with information about wetland plants and habitats.
A limestone cliff above Bajót with caves and steep rock walls. A stepped path leads to the top, overlooking the surrounding hills.
A cave in the Öreg-kő cliffs with a large chamber and an opening in its ceiling, known for prehistoric archaeological finds.
The highest peak of the Gerecse (634 m), surrounded by beech woodland. A forest path leads to the top through the rocky interior of the range.
The Turul monument on a rocky viewpoint above Tatabánya, overlooking the city and nearby hills, with Szelim Cave a short walk away.
A large cave chamber above Tatabánya with openings in its ceiling and a natural rock window overlooking the city and surrounding landscape.
A lake beside the castle in historic Tata, with a shoreline walking path past reed beds and bird habitats, overlooking the water.
Water castle on the shore of Öreg-tó, built by King Sigismund and extended by King Matthias. It houses the Kuny Domokos Museum.
Baroque palace of the Esterházy family in Tata, designed by Jakab Fellner. Reopened after restoration, its halls house exhibitions.
A cave entrance on a rocky slope of the Gerecse, reached by a forest path among limestone outcrops showing the rocks of the range.
A wooded hill above Tardos where several Gerecse hiking routes meet, with traces of quarrying and woodland paths in the surrounding area.
An elevated walkway among the trees near Tardos, with views of the canopy, tree trunks and the surrounding woodland from above ground level.
A forest clearing on the slope of the Gerecse with a rain shelter and a rest area, reached by several hiking routes through beech woodland.
An arboretum in a stream valley among the Gerecse woods, with a conifer collection, ponds and shaded paths through the grounds.
A granite boulder among the Pákozd rocking stones, with rounded surfaces shaped by weather, reached on a woodland walking path.
